quotes.text: Ragh isn't a new model. It's not a bigger or better GPT. It's a different approach entirely.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects a common misconception about what RAG is.

quotes.text: The LLM never sees your raw data. It only sees what the retrieval system hands it. It's not a drawback, so it's a security feature. Your sensitive documents stay in your own storage.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the data-protection benefit of the RAG pattern in plain words.

quotes.text: Fine tuning is like teaching someone a textbook by heart. Useful, but they still can't look up today's newspaper.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable analogy for why fine-tuning does not solve stale knowledge.

quotes.text: Make sure your retrieval works perfectly before you add the LLM. Most Ragn failures aren't model problems, they're retrieval problems.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear, actionable recommendation for building RAG solutions.

takeaways: RAG first retrieves relevant content from your own data and passes it to the model with the question, so answers are current and grounded instead of guessed from training memory.
On Azure, Azure AI Search indexes and retrieves chunks with vector or hybrid search, Azure OpenAI generates the answer, and Azure AI Foundry wires the agent together.
Start with your data, get retrieval right before adding the LLM, and choose agentic RAG only for complex questions where accuracy is worth the extra tokens and latency.
hook: Large language models do not know your company's data and their knowledge is frozen in time. This Simply Explained episode shows developers, architects and IT pros how retrieval-augmented generation on Azure solves that with Azure AI Search, Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Foundry, and how to start building it the right way.
